name: Grouper
label: Kranky
lede: Liz Harris grew up in a commune called The Group, named her music after it, and has spent twenty years making songs so buried in tape hiss that a microwave beep and a fever both ended up part of the records.

eras.title: A childhood inside The Group
eras.text: Liz Harris was born in Northern California in 1980 and raised around the Bay Area in a Fourth Way commune based on the teachings of George Gurdjieff. She studied art at UC Berkeley and worked with Mayo Thompson at the Patrick Painter gallery in Los Angeles before the music took over.

years.h: Liz Harris is born and raised in a Gurdjieff commune called The Group
years.p: Harris grew up in a Fourth Way commune known as The Group. Kids and parents there called each other groupers, which later became her project's name.
years.xp: Harris has said the children used the word grouper as a small act of defiance inside a controlled environment. When she started recording, the name fit a second way: she felt the music at its barest was just a grouping of sounds, and she was the grouper.

eras.title: Tape hiss in Portland
eras.text: Working out of Portland, Oregon, Liz Harris released CD-Rs and small-label records of guitar, voice and loops smeared into fog. The UK label Type picked her up, and Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill made people realize there were songs in there.

years.p: Liz Harris self-releases a CD-R debut, then Way Their Crept, which the UK label Type reissues in 2007.

years.h: Wide, and a collaboration with Xiu Xiu
years.p: Grouper's third album arrives, along with Creepshow, a collaboration with [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]].
Another Grouper album of drones and half-heard vocals, the last before the record that changed things.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill
years.h: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill: Grouper's breakthrough on Type
years.p: The cover is a childhood photo of Liz Harris taken by her mother. Stereogum later called it her first set of songs that sound like songs.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Mike McGonigal gave it 8.2 and called it an arresting album of pastoral psychedelic pop. Ten years on, Pitchfork put it at No. 6 on its list of the best dream pop albums. Kranky reissued it in 2013.
play: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill

eras.title: Double albums, sleep cycles and a mirror
eras.text: Grouper started her own label, Yellow Electric, for a two-part album, then pushed into long-form tape collage and an eight-hour piece built around sleep. Her first Kranky release came through a duo with Tiny Vipers.

years.h: A I A: Dream Loss and Alien Observer on Yellow Electric
years.p: Liz Harris issues a two-part album on her own label. Pitchfork later ranked Alien Observer 21st among the best ambient albums ever.

years.h: Mirrorring: Liz Harris and Tiny Vipers' Jesy Fortino on Kranky
years.p: After touring Europe together, Harris and [[Jesy Fortino|e37d27dd-7d69-4f60-964b-397669364841]] form Mirrorring, spelled with a doubled r for symmetry. Foreign Body is Harris's first album on Kranky.

years.h: Circular Veil: an eight-hour piece shaped like a night's sleep
years.p: With [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]], Liz Harris premieres an eight-hour installation at Berlin's Club Transmediale that follows a full sleep cycle. She also tours Europe performing the tape-collage work Violet Replacement.

eras.title: A boat on Agate Beach, a beep in Portugal
eras.text: Now on Kranky, Grouper cleared out her vaults and released a piano record made in a borrowed house in Portugal. It became her most acclaimed album, and she branched into film, opera-house commissions and festival curation.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Man Who Died in His Boat
years.h: The Man Who Died in His Boat: Liz Harris's teenage memory
years.p: Grouper's first solo Kranky album gathers outtakes from the Dragging a Dead Deer sessions. The title comes from a sailboat wreck Harris saw washed up at Agate Beach in Bolinas as a teenager.
years.xp:
Harris walked down with her father to look inside the cabin and said she felt she was violating what was left of the man by witnessing it. According to Wikipedia, the boat likely belonged to Dr. William Groppe, whose fully provisioned sailboat was found off Agate Beach in August 1998; he was declared dead in absentia that October while sailing for Hawaii.

Pitchfork named the single Vital a Best New Track. Kranky also reissued Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill and the A I A albums that year.

years.h: Ruins: piano, a 4-track and a microwave beep in Portugal
years.p: Liz Harris recorded Ruins in 2011 during a residency in Aljezur, Portugal, on a portable 4-track and an upright piano. When a storm cut the power, a microwave beeped, and she left it on the end of Labyrinth.
years.xp: The house belonged to the aunt of music director Sérgio Hydalgo; the residency was organized by Galeria Zé dos Bois. The last track was recorded separately at her mother's house in 2004. Pitchfork gave Ruins Best New Music and ranked it the fifth best album of 2014.

years.h: Grouper features on The Bug's Angels & Devils
years.p: Liz Harris sings on Void and Black Wasp for [[Kevin Martin|ac853422-64b8-493f-96cd-3eb0b209b8aa]]'s The Bug, and starts the trio Helen with Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmons.

years.h: Hypnosis Display with filmmaker Paul Clipson for Opera North
years.p: Leeds' Opera North commissions Liz Harris and San Francisco filmmaker Paul Clipson for a live film-and-music piece. Helen releases The Original Faces the same year.

years.h: Liz Harris curates Le Guess Who? in Utrecht
years.p: For the festival's 11th edition, Grouper programs [[William Basinski|3b731282-d7f4-41a5-af0a-d0c1c3319802]], Keiji Haino and Richard Youngs, plus Kieślowski's The Double Life of Véronique and Paul Clipson's Lighthouse.

eras.title: Twenty-two minutes, then fifteen years
eras.text: Grouper's next Kranky record was an album she stopped making when she got sick, and she refused to pad it. The one after collected songs from fifteen years of recording. In between she stepped out under a new name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grid of Points · Wikipedia: Grouper (musician)
years.h: Grid of Points: 22 minutes, finished by a fever
years.p: Liz Harris wrote and recorded it in about a week and a half at the Ucross Foundation in Wyoming in 2014, snowed in by a cold snap, until a fever stopped her. Kranky worried it was too short; she wouldn't add anything.
years.xp: The first single, Parking Lot, arrived on March 8, 2018, and was named one of NPR's Songs We Love and a Pitchfork Best New Track. The album runs 21 minutes and 52 seconds and scored 80 on Metacritic.

years.h: Nivhek: Liz Harris records under a new name
years.p: Harris releases After Its Own Death / Walking in a Spiral Towards the House as Nivhek on her Yellow Electric label, her first major work outside the Grouper name.

years.h: Shade: Grouper songs from fifteen years of recording
years.p: Announced with the single Unclean Mind on July 27, 2021, Grouper's Kranky album collects songs Liz Harris recorded over the previous fifteen years.

Liz Harris and [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]] release a second Raum album, nine years after The Event of Your Leaving. Harris now lives in Astoria, Oregon, where she runs an exhibition space.
